schemaNotes.gradientsPct: gradientsPct[i] = mean gradient (%) of segment i; segments are resolutionM long except the last, which is lengthM - resolutionM*(n-1) (may be shorter).
schemaNotes.elevations: startElevationM is measured (real climbs: DEM along the road) or designed (fictional loops). endElevationM and gainM are recomputed from gradientsPct, so they are internally consistent with the table.
schemaNotes.turns: atKm = distance from route start. kind: hairpin (>=135 deg heading change within ~100 m), sharp (75-135 deg), bend (<75 deg, fictional routes only), loop (270 deg self-crossing). angleDeg = approximate heading change. label = signed/known name where available.
schemaNotes.published: Reference figures from the cited sources, kept for cross-checking; they differ slightly between sources because of different start/finish points.
schemaNotes.fictional: Routes with country 'Fictional' are designed loops (loop=true); gradients net to 0 m.

routes.name: Alpe d'Huez
routes.description: The D211 from Bourg d'Oisans climbs ~1,135 m in 14 km through 21 numbered hairpins (Virage 21 at the bottom to Virage 1 at the resort entrance), each signed with the names of Tour de France stage winners. After a flat 0.6 km across the valley floor, the first ~3.5 km up to La Garde are the steepest (10-11%); the rest settles into a steady 7.5-9.5% to the ski resort.
routes.scenery: Steep limestone valley walls of the Romanche valley, terraced pasture and hamlets (La Garde, Huez village church), switchback walls with stone parapets, ski-resort chalets at the top; views over Bourg d'Oisans and the Écrins massif.

start.label: D211 at the Bourg d'Oisans roundabout (valley floor, ~720 m)

finish.label: Top of Avenue du Rif Nel, Alpe d'Huez (~1,855 m)

published.notes: Wikipedia/RCUK: 13.8 km, 8.1%, max 13%, summit 1,860 m. Climbfinder: 14.3 km, 717-1859 m, 7.9%, max 14%. Biketips: Virage 21 at 806 m, Virage 17 at 965 m (our DEM: 814 m and 962 m).

routes.curvatureNotes: 21 numbered hairpins between km 1.5 and km 12.1, spaced ~0.15-0.9 km apart (Virage 20/19 are a tight pair at km 2.2-2.4), plus two unnumbered hairpins inside the resort (km 12.9, 13.2) and six sharp bends. Short straights between hairpins; ~6-7 m wide road with stone parapets.

routes.name: Mont Ventoux (Bédoin)
routes.description: The classic D974 ascent from Bédoin: an easy first 6 km through vineyards to Saint-Estève, then ~9 km at 9-10% through dense forest to Chalet Reynard (~km 15, ~1,420 m), and a final 6 km across bare white limestone scree past the Tom Simpson memorial to the summit observatory at ~1,910 m.
routes.scenery: Provençal vineyards, cherry orchards and stone villages around Bédoin; dense oak, pine and cedar forest in the middle section; above Chalet Reynard a treeless white limestone 'moonscape' with the red-and-white observatory tower on the skyline; often windy (mistral).

start.label: Bédoin, start of the D974 Route du Mont-Ventoux (~300-310 m)

finish.label: Summit road beside the observatory/weather station (1,909-1,910 m; DEM reads ~1,899 m)

published.notes: Epic Road Rides: 21.3 km, 1,579 m, 7.4%. Col Collective: 21.8 km, 1,629 m, 7.4%, max 12%. Provence Guide: Bédoin-Saint-Estève 5.5 km @ ~4.5%, Saint-Estève-Chalet Reynard 8 km @ ~9.4%, final 6 km @ ~8%. Ours: 21.4 km, 1,587 m, 7.4%, Chalet Reynard at km 15.1 (DEM 1,429 m vs signed 1,419 m).

routes.curvatureNotes: Few true hairpins: sharp left at Saint-Estève where the steep forest section begins (km 5.6), a hairpin in the forest (km 10.3), the left turn at Chalet Reynard (km 15.1), long sweeping curves across the bare upper slopes, and the famous final right-hand hairpin ~200 m below the summit (km 21.2).
routes.notes: Summit DEM is ~10 m low (sharp peak smoothed by the 30 m DEM); real road top is 1,909-1,910 m.

routes.name: Col du Tourmalet (west side, from Luz-Saint-Sauveur)
routes.description: The west side of the Tourmalet on the D918, from Luz-Saint-Sauveur through the spa village of Barèges (~km 7) and past Super-Barèges into open high pasture to the col at 2,115 m. A steady 7-8% most of the way, steepening to ~9-10% in the last 3-4 km; the Tourmalet is the most-used climb in Tour de France history.
routes.scenery: Narrow Bastan valley with stone villages and slate roofs, beech and fir forest below Barèges, then treeless green alpine pasture with grazing sheep and horses, snow fences and avalanche barriers, rocky peaks and the Pic du Midi observatory above; the 'Géant du Tourmalet' cyclist statue at the col.

start.label: Luz-Saint-Sauveur, D918 at the Pont de Luz junction (~711 m)

published.notes: Cols-cyclisme / Wikipedia / RCUK: 19.0 km, 711 -> 2,115 m, 1,404 m, 7.4%, max 10.2% (some sources list 13% for short ramps). Rouvy: 18.7 km, 1,399 m. Ours: 18.9 km, 715 -> 2,118 m, 1,403 m, 7.4%.

routes.curvatureNotes: Long sweeping valley road; three tight S-bend pairs crossing side ravines (km 4.0-4.2, 5.4-5.6, 6.7-6.8); slow bends through Barèges (km 7-7.5); a cluster of hairpins above Super-Barèges (km 11.0-12.9) and three big switchbacks in the final 4 km (km 14.8, 17.1, 18.5).

routes.name: Passo dello Stelvio (from Prato allo Stelvio)
routes.description: The SS38 north ramp from Prato allo Stelvio (Prad) climbs ~1,840 m in 24.5 km through Gomagoi and Trafoi and then up the famous stacked wall of 48 numbered hairpins (tornanti) to the pass at 2,757 m, the highest paved pass in the Eastern Alps and a frequent Cima Coppi of the Giro d'Italia.
routes.scenery: Vinschgau apple orchards at the bottom, a narrow wooded gorge to Gomagoi, larch and spruce forest around Trafoi with the glaciated Ortler (3,905 m) towering above, then bare scree, snowfields and the stacked hairpins; hotels and snack stands at the summit, snow walls early in the season.

start.label: Prato allo Stelvio / Prad am Stilfser Joch, start of the SS38 pass road (~915 m)

finish.label: Passo dello Stelvio / Stilfser Joch (2,757 m)

published.notes: Road.cc / RCUK: ~24.3 km, ~1,808 m, 7.4%; Sportive Breaks: 24.5 km, 1,824 m, 7.4%; start quoted 909-934 m; summit 2,757-2,758 m; 48 numbered hairpins starting ~8 km above Prad and ending a few hundred metres below the top (cycloclimbing.com); max 13% (some sources 15-16% for short ramps). Ours: 24.5 km, 914 -> 2,756 m, 1,843 m, 7.5%, 48 hairpins detected from km 8.0 to km 24.1.

routes.curvatureNotes: Valley road with gentle curves for the first ~8 km; the 48 hairpins run from km 8.0 to km 24.1, sparse to Trafoi (km ~11) and then dense in the final 11 km where they come every 100-500 m. Hairpin labels (Tornante 48 -> 1) were assigned in order of geometric detection; the detected count matches the signed count of 48.

routes.name: Sa Calobra (Coll dels Reis)
routes.description: The Ma-2141, built in 1932 to engineer Antoni Parietti's design, climbs from the cove of Sa Calobra up a limestone gorge to the Coll dels Reis (682 m) in just under 10 km at a steady ~7%, with 26 hairpins and the 'Nus de sa Corbata' (necktie knot), where the road loops 270 degrees and passes under itself.

turns.label: Nus de sa Corbata (270-degree loop; road passes under itself at ~km 9.03/9.20)

routes.scenery: Turquoise Mediterranean cove at the mouth of the Torrent de Pareis gorge, grey karst limestone cliffs and pinnacles, holm oak, wild olive and dwarf palm scrub, wild goats; the serpentine road visible coiling below you as you climb.

start.label: Sa Calobra, foot of the Ma-2141 by the port car park

published.notes: RCUK: 9.4 km, ~7%, 682 m top, 26 hairpins, max 11%. Biketips: 9.5 km, 643 m, 6.8%, max 13.4%. Climbfinder: ~10 km at 7%, top 723 m, steepest 100 m 11.1%. Altigraphs: 10.18 km, 22 -> 725 m. Pass altitude 682 m (Wikipedia). Published gains span 643-682 m. Ours: 9.76 km, 17 -> 682 m, 666 m, 6.8%.

routes.curvatureNotes: Tight and twisty throughout: 18 hairpins (>=135 deg) and 17 sharp bends detected (the published count is 26 hairpins), concentrated between km 5.7 and 9.1. The Nus de sa Corbata 270-degree loop is at ~km 9.0-9.2: the road passes over its own earlier section on a small bridge.

routes.name: Mount Diablo (South Gate, Mount Diablo Challenge route)
routes.region: East Bay, Contra Costa County, CA
routes.description: The Mount Diablo Challenge course from Athenian School in Danville: Mt Diablo Scenic Blvd and South Gate Rd wind up through oak savanna to the Junction ranger station (~2,170 ft, km 11), then Summit Rd climbs the open ridge to the 3,849 ft summit, finishing with a short ~15% ramp into the summit parking lot.
routes.scenery: Golden summer grass (green in winter/spring), blue and valley oak savanna, chaparral and grey pine, sandstone outcrops at Rock City, wide views over the Central Valley, the Bay and on clear days the Sierra Nevada; the stone summit visitor centre and beacon.

start.label: Mt Diablo Scenic Blvd at Blackhawk Rd, Danville (Athenian School; ~590 ft)

finish.label: Summit parking lot / visitor centre (~3,830-3,849 ft)

published.notes: Save Mount Diablo / event listings: Mount Diablo Challenge 11.2 mi (18.0 km), 3,249 ft (990 m), ~5.7% (one listing gives 10.8 mi). Summit 3,849 ft. Ours: 18.16 km (11.3 mi), 180 -> 1,168 m, 989 m gain (3,245 ft), 5.4%, Junction at km 11.0 (DEM 663 m).

routes.curvatureNotes: Constant curvature: South Gate Rd has many tight bends and switchbacks (hairpins at ~km 1.5, 2.1, 2.8-3.1, 3.8, 4.2, 4.5, 5.2, 7.7-8.0); Summit Rd above the Junction is a sequence of ridge switchbacks (km 10.6-12.2, 13.8, 14.7, 16.7, 17.5). The first 1.8 km on Mt Diablo Scenic Blvd are a gently rising residential lane.
routes.notes: North Gate (from Walnut Creek) joins at the Junction; this entry is the South Gate side. A short dip around km 7 (-0.2%) is real (Rock City area).

routes.name: Mount Tamalpais East Peak (from Tam Junction, Mill Valley)
routes.description: Sea level to the East Peak of Mount Tamalpais: Shoreline Hwy and Panoramic Hwy climb steadily (~6.5%) through eucalyptus and redwood, roll gently past Mountain Home to Pantoll, then Pantoll Rd and East Ridgecrest Blvd climb the open ridge to a high point near West Peak (~2,500 ft) before a short drop and final kick into the East Peak lot.
routes.scenery: Coastal fog banks over the Pacific and Stinson Beach, redwood and Douglas fir groves along Panoramic Hwy, then open serpentine grassland, manzanita and rock outcrops along Ridgecrest with views of San Francisco, the Golden Gate and the Bay; the East Peak fire lookout above the final car park.

start.label: Tam Junction (Shoreline Hwy / CA-1 at Almonte Blvd), Mill Valley, ~sea level

finish.label: East Peak parking lot (~2,350 ft; the peak itself is a short hike to 2,571 ft)

published.notes: No published climb uses exactly this start/finish. PJAMM 'Mt. Tam via Hwy 1 South' (Panoramic, to the summit area): 10.3 mi, 2,675-2,724 ft, 4.6-4.7%. PJAMM Muir Woods Rd -> Pantoll leg of Panoramic: 4.5 mi, 960 ft, 3.2%. East Ridgecrest Blvd ~3 mi (Hydrapak). East Peak 2,571-2,574 ft. Ours: 19.7 km (12.3 mi), 3 -> 715 m, 787 m (2,582 ft) total gain; road high point ~752 m (table) / 761 m (raw DEM) at km 17.4-17.5.

routes.curvatureNotes: Two hairpins on Shoreline Hwy above Tam Junction (km 2.0, 2.5), a hairpin at the Panoramic turn-off (km 4.3); Panoramic Hwy is continuously curvy with a hairpin cluster near Pantoll (km 10.9-11.7); Pantoll Rd and Ridgecrest are sinuous ridge-top roads with frequent sharp bends (41 detected).
routes.notes: Rolling middle section (km 5-10, -3% to +7%) and a 1.5 km descent at km 17.4-19.3 make this a 'climb with rests' rather than a steady ascent. Ridgecrest Blvd gates close at night.

routes.name: Old La Honda Road
routes.description: The Peninsula's benchmark climb, reputedly the most-ridden Strava segment: a narrow, shaded, mostly one-lane road climbing 3.3 miles through redwoods and oaks at a remarkably steady 7-8% from Portola Rd in Woodside to the stop sign at Skyline Blvd. Bay Area riders use their OLH time as a fitness yardstick.
routes.scenery: Second-growth redwood, bay laurel and live oak canopy, ferns and mossy banks, a creek and stone bridge at the bottom, occasional wooden gates and mailboxes; cool, quiet and dappled light.

start.label: Old La Honda Rd at Portola Rd, Woodside (stone bridge just beyond)

published.notes: Strava full-climb segments 3.28-3.30 mi; ride write-up: 3 mi, 1,295 ft to Skyline (~8% from the bridge); PJAMM: steepest quarter mile 8.8%. Ours: 5.29 km (3.29 mi), 118 -> 515 m, 397 m (1,302 ft), 7.5%.

routes.curvatureNotes: Very twisty narrow road: constant tight curves, three switchback-like hairpins (km 0.5, 1.4, 3.6) and frequent sharp bends; few straights longer than ~100 m. Good candidate for high road-curvature rendering with low speed.

routes.name: Claremont Avenue to the Summit (Grizzly Peak Blvd)
routes.description: The East Bay's signature canyon climb: Claremont Ave starts gently from College Ave past the Claremont Hotel, then steepens up Claremont Canyon, with the final ~1.5 km averaging 10-12% (short ramps steeper) to 'the Summit' junction with Grizzly Peak Blvd and Fish Ranch Rd.
routes.scenery: Elmwood craftsman houses and the white Claremont Hotel, then eucalyptus, oak and coastal scrub in Claremont Canyon; views back over Oakland, the Bay Bridge and San Francisco from the top.

finish.label: The Summit: Claremont Ave / Grizzly Peak Blvd / Fish Ranch Rd (~1,305 ft)

published.notes: bikeclimbs.com 'Claremont - College to Grizzly Peak': 3.98 km, 333.6 m, 8.4%; 'Claremont to Grizzly Peak Blvd': 3.8 km, 318.7 m, 8.4%, max 17.6% (short ramp). PJAMM 'Grizzly Peak (Claremont)' continues north along Grizzly Peak Blvd to 1,665 ft: 3.6 mi, 1,325 ft, 6.9%. Ours: 4.53 km, 63 -> 398 m, 335 m, 7.4% (length differs from bikeclimbs by ~0.5 km; gain matches).

routes.curvatureNotes: Straight urban avenue for 1.5 km, a right-hand bend at the Ashby Ave/Claremont Hotel junction (km 1.5), then gentle canyon curves with a few sharper bends in the steep upper section (km 3.7, 4.1). No hairpins.

routes.name: South Park Drive (Tilden)
routes.region: Tilden Regional Park, Berkeley Hills, CA
routes.description: A short, steep and quiet climb through Tilden Regional Park from Wildcat Canyon Rd up to Grizzly Peak Blvd: about 2.3 km at ~9.4%, with the middle kilometre at 10-12%. It closes to motor vehicles each winter (roughly Nov 1 to early April) for the California newt migration.
routes.scenery: Monterey pine and eucalyptus groves, oak woodland and grassy slopes; newts crossing after winter rains; glimpses east toward Mount Diablo near the top.

start.label: South Park Dr at Wildcat Canyon Rd, Tilden Park

finish.label: South Park Dr at Grizzly Peak Blvd

published.notes: No reliable published length/gain found in search; the East Bay Regional Park District confirms the annual winter newt closure (2025-26: Nov 1 - Apr 2). Ours: 2.28 km, 288 -> 504 m, 215 m, 9.4%.

routes.curvatureNotes: Gently winding forest road with one sharper left bend (~km 1.7); no hairpins.

routes.name: Hawk Hill (Conzelman Road)
routes.region: Marin Headlands, Golden Gate NRA, CA
routes.description: The short, scenic climb just north of the Golden Gate Bridge: Conzelman Rd rises ~165 m in 2.8 km (~5.8%) along the Marin Headlands cliffs to the top of Hawk Hill (~248 m / 814 ft), with the bridge towers and the San Francisco skyline beside you most of the way.
routes.scenery: Golden Gate Bridge towers at eye level, the San Francisco skyline and the Bay, coastal scrub and wildflowers, WWII-era gun batteries, fog pouring through the Golden Gate; migrating hawks in autumn (a well-known raptor-watch site).

start.label: Conzelman Rd at Alexander Ave, north end of the Golden Gate Bridge

finish.label: Top of Hawk Hill on Conzelman Rd (~248 m / 814 ft)

published.notes: PJAMM: 1.8 mi, 538 ft, 5.8%. Climbfinder: 1.8 mi, 541 ft, 5.7%, steepest segment 11.5%, top 814 ft (248 m). Ours: 2.84 km, 84 -> 248 m, 164 m, 5.8%.

routes.notes: Beyond the top, Conzelman Rd becomes a one-way steep descent toward Point Bonita (not included).

routes.name: Fogline Coast Loop
routes.region: Fictional Pacific coastline (inspired by the Marin/Sonoma coast)
routes.description: A rolling 28 km coastal loop over seven grassy headlands between sandy coves: repeated 0.75-1.25 km rises at 4-6% and swooping descents, separated by flat stretches along beaches and a lagoon, with about 330 m of total climbing.
routes.scenery: Palette: Pacific blues (deep #1E4E6E, shallows #6FA8C9) with white surf lines, marine-layer fog (#DDE3E6) drifting over the bluffs, golden coastal grassland (#C9A86A), coyote brush and lupine scrub (#6B7F5A), dark Monterey cypress windbreaks (#2E3B30), weathered fence posts, sea stacks with cormorants, and a white lighthouse on the far point. Ambient: surf, gulls, foghorn.
routes.curvatureNotes: The road hugs the bluff edge, curving over the headlands with sharper 75-95 deg bends where it wraps around coves, and runs straighter on the beach flats. Clockwise loop; ~40 turn cues summing to ~+360 deg.
routes.notes: Fictional route: the profile is designed, not measured. 'confidence' refers to internal consistency (closure, gradient limits), not to a real-world match.

routes.region: Fictional high desert (inspired by the Oregon high desert / Colorado Plateau)
routes.description: A wide-open 36 km high-desert loop of long, steady drags (2-5% for 2-4 km) up to mesa rims, with gradual runs back down across sagebrush flats; about 335 m of total climbing under big skies.
routes.scenery: Palette: sagebrush silver-green (#9AA58A), western juniper (#4A5D3F), red and ochre rimrock and mesa cliffs (#B5653D, #D39A5B), pale dry washes (#E3D3B0), a distant snow-capped volcanic cone, cobalt sky (#3D7CC9) with cumulus, long purple dusk shadows (#6E5A8A). Ambient: wind, meadowlarks, distant hawk.
routes.curvatureNotes: Long straights with gentle 10-70 deg sweepers and a few bends where the road drops through dry washes; no hairpins. Clockwise loop; turn cues sum to ~+360 deg.
routes.notes: Fictional route: the profile is designed, not measured. 'confidence' refers to internal consistency (closure, gradient limits), not to a real-world match.
routes.profileSource: Synthetic: generated by research tools/synth.py (deterministic seed). Elevation = mid-wavelength (1.2-6 km) periodic texture + asymmetric smooth rise/plateau/fall features, sampled as 250 m chord gradients, rounded to 0.1% and nudged so the loop closes to 0 m net. Turn cues are synthetic, with signed angles summing to ~+360 deg (one clockwise lap).
